newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire denies its troops attacked Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Zaire denies its troops attacked Uganda.

text.p: Zaire denied on Wednesday that its troops had attacked positions in Uganda in alliance with Zaire-based Ugandan rebels.
"It's in their imagination," government spokesman Boguo Makeli told Reuters in reaction to Uganda's charges of attacks on two of its southwestern border posts on Wednesday.
Boguo, who is information minister, instead repeated Zaire's allegations that Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi were fighting with ethnic Tutsi rebels who have seized part of eastern Zaire.
"It is Zaire that is being attacked. Uganda has made up the story in order to justify in the eyes of the world the murderous acts which they have been party to in east Zaire," he said.

In a statement in the name of the Ugandan cabinet, minister of state for international cooperation Martin Aliker said Uganda had repulsed the "enemy" and the Zairean soldiers and Ugandan dissidents retreated into Zaire from where they shelled Ugandan positions all day.
It added that Uganda had reinforced its positions and its army would defend its territorial integrity at all times.
